First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}-3X+4 \\  & ={X}^{2}-3X+4I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(B)={B}^{2}-3B+4I.$

Let's calculate ${B}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{2} & =B\cdot B \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -9 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(B):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(B) & ={B}^{2}-3B+4I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -9 & 7\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]+4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -9 & 7\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ -9 & 6\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4-3+4 & -3-(-3)+0 \\ -9-(-9)+0 & 7-6+4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
